fault_line: Siege or security checkpoint? The Ansar Allah leader says food and medicine flow freely and only weapons are blocked -- HRW and OCHA say a city is being starved. Who do the roads prove right?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM - the denial] Ansar Allah leader Abdel-Malik al-Ansar Allah denied his forces are besieging Taiz, claiming only the entry of weapons is prohibited: 'The way is open for food supplies, medicine, and humanitarian necessities to enter the city of Taiz, even for the groups affiliated with the Saudis.' Context in the same entry: Taiz has been cut off since early October, losing both land routes after al-Turbah fell by Oct 4, severing the Taiz-Al-Turbah-Aden road; OCHA warns 'time is running out' for the 800,000 people trapped inside. This directly contests HRW's Oct 29 finding (1800-01) that the siege may amount to the war crime of starvation.
sections.what_verified: Single declared family: Al Jazeera (T2, STATE-QA) reporting the speech. The denial itself is a primary-source claim; its truth is contested by HRW + OCHA material already on record, not corroborated here.
sections.what_disputed: HRW (1800-01): full encirclement since October 2026, 600,000+ cut off from aid, may amount to war crime of starvation. OCHA (via AJ, same entry): 800,000 trapped, 'time is running out'. Taiz Human Rights Centre (Oct 28, via 1900-window entry): siege on Kahlan + obstruction of ambulances, medical aid, food and medicine. Note the trapped-population figures differ by source (HRW 600,000+ cut off vs OCHA 800,000 trapped) -- scope differs; do not merge them.
sections.why_matters: 'We are not besieging Taiz': the Ansar Allah leader answers HRW's war-crime finding head-on -- denial vs the 800,000 trapped, in his own words vs OCHA's
